item.title: Bank of England's Mann says high inflation has become embedded in UK
item.description: Inflation running above the Bank of England's 2% target appears to have become embedded in the British economy, BoE policymaker Catherine Mann said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Inflation running above the Bank of England's 2% target appears to have become embedded in the British economy, BoE policymaker Catherine Mann said on Tuesday. "We've had inflation well above target for the entire time I've been in my position.... Inflation has become embedded," she said at a conference hosted by economic advisors TS Lombard. Mann added that she was particularly concerned that inflation looked set to hit 4% around the turn of the year, the most common period for employers and workers to negotiate wage increases, potentially further entrenching price rises. Since July, Mann has been part of a minority on the BoE Monetary Policy Committee voting for a quarter-point rise in interest rates to 4%.

item.title: Italy regulator probes AI music startup Suno over terms of service
item.description: Italy's antitrust authority said on Tuesday it had opened an investigation into AI music startup Suno, saying some clauses in its terms of service may be unfair to consumers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy's antitrust authority said on Tuesday it had opened an investigation into AI music startup Suno, saying some clauses in its terms of service may be unfair to consumers. Suno was not immediately available for comment Suno's terms could create a significant imbalance in the rights and obligations of users, the watchdog said They give Suno "broad discretion" to unilaterally modify its contract, service and subscription prices without having to provide any justification, it added in a statement The regulator said the licence granted by users was excessively broad and included a waiver of moral rights that may conflict with Italian copyright law Suno's terms require users to resolve disputes through mandatory arbitration in the United States, waive class-action rights and accept Massachusetts as the exclusive jurisdiction for legal claims, the authority said It added it would launch a consultation in the coming weeks in which interested business groups, chambers of commerce and consumer associations could participate

item.title: Argentina, Uruguay, Chile y Brasil presentan una candidatura para organizar el Mundial de Rugby de 2035
item.description: Argentina, Uruguay, Chile y Brasil presentaron una candidatura conjunta para organizar el Mundial de Rugby de 2035, con la aspiración de llevar por primera vez a Sudamérica el torneo que se disputa cada cuatro años, dijo el lunes la Unión Argentina de Rugby (UAR).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Argentina, Uruguay, Chile y Brasil presentaron una candidatura conjunta para organizar el Mundial de Rugby de 2035, con la aspiración de llevar por primera vez a Sudamérica el torneo que se disputa cada cuatro años, dijo el lunes la Unión Argentina de Rugby (UAR). La candidatura contempla disputar partidos en 11 estadios de 10 ciudades, con ocho recintos en Argentina y uno en cada uno de los otros tres países: el Estadio Centenario de Montevideo, el Estadio Nacional de Santiago de Chile y el emblemático Maracaná de Rio de Janeiro. España y Japón también han expresado interés en organizar el torneo. World Rugby realizará visitas a las sedes y evaluaciones de viabilidad antes de seleccionar una candidatura preferida a más tardar en mayo próximo, y se espera una decisión definitiva en noviembre de 2027. "Tenemos la oportunidad de mostrarle al mundo nuestra pasión por este deporte, nuestra capacidad para organizar grandes eventos y todo lo que nuestros países pueden ofrecer", dijo el presidente de la UAR, Félix Páez Molina, en un comunicado. "Es un desafío que asumimos con la profunda convicción de que nuestra región se merece una oportunidad de esta magnitud", dijo Páez. "Es un proyecto que nos entusiasma y que estamos construyendo junto a las Uniones de la región y Sudamérica Rugby, con la aspiración de que, por primera vez, una Rugby World Cup pueda disputarse en esta parte del mundo". El próximo Mundial se celebrará en Australia en 2027, y el torneo llegará por primera vez al continente americano en 2031, cuando se dispute en Estados Unidos. Argentina es el país con mejores resultados en el rugby de América: los Pumas han alcanzado las semifinales del Mundial en tres ocasiones, en 2007, 2015 y 2023. Uruguay ha participado en cinco ediciones, mientras que Chile debutó en 2023 y Brasil aún no ha logrado clasificarse para el torneo.

item.title: Sinner se perderá lo que queda de 2026 para recuperarse de una lesión de rodilla
item.description: El tenista número uno del mundo, Jannik Sinner, no volverá a competir en 2026 tras decidir continuar con su recuperación de una lesión de rodilla que le ha mantenido fuera de las pistas desde su triunfal participación en Wimbledon el pasado mes de julio.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El tenista número uno del mundo, Jannik Sinner, no volverá a competir en 2026 tras decidir continuar con su recuperación de una lesión de rodilla que le ha mantenido fuera de las pistas desde su triunfal participación en Wimbledon el pasado mes de julio. "Siguiendo el consejo de su equipo médico, Jannik Sinner se someterá a un tratamiento para la inflamación de la rodilla", ha declarado el equipo de Sinner en un comunicado. "Se ha tomado la decisión de someterse al tratamiento ahora para que Jannik disponga del tiempo necesario para recuperarse antes de comenzar los preparativos para 2027. Por consiguiente, Jannik no podrá volver a competir durante la temporada 2026".

item.title: Toronto home sales post steepest decline since February on economic uncertainty
item.description: Greater Toronto Area home sales fell by the most in seven months in September as economic uncertainty held back buyers, Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data showed on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: Greater Toronto Area home sales fell by the most in seven months in September as economic uncertainty held back buyers, Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data showed on Tuesday. Seasonally adjusted sales decreased 5.2% last month from August to 5,174 units, marking the second straight month of decline and the steepest drop since February. The board's home price index was down 0.5% month-over-month, after seasonal adjustment, to C$924,600 ($648,296). The Greater Toronto Area (GTA) includes Canada's most populous city and four surrounding regional municipalities. “We know there is substantial pent-up demand in the GTA, with many households fully intending on purchasing a home in the months ahead," the board's chief information officer, Jason Mercer, said in a statement. "These would-be homebuyers want to take advantage of today’s more affordable housing market, but they need to be confident that their employment situation will remain solid and inflation will not put pressure on borrowing costs over the long term,” Mercer said. [USN:L6N44U0U8 TEXT:"Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem"] has said that policymakers were prepared to raise borrowing costs multiple times if inflation remained too high. On a year-over-year basis, home sales fell 9%, while new listings declined 14.4% and the price index was down 4.7%. ($1 = 1.4262 Canadian dollars)

item.title: Most Americans support switch to Medicare for all health insurance
item.description: Most Americans now favor government-paid health insurance for all, according to a new poll, as voters across party lines see major healthcare reforms as a priority less than a month before midterm elections to decide control of the US Congress.
item.dc:creator: Amina Niasse
item.content:encoded: Most Americans now favor government-paid health insurance for all, according to a new poll, as voters across party lines see major healthcare reforms as a priority less than a month before midterm elections to decide control of the US Congress. Two-thirds of US adults — up from 53% in 2020 — said they are in favor of universal US health insurance often referred to as "Medicare for all," according to a poll conducted by health policy research firm KFF released on Tuesday. By party affiliation, 84% of respondents who identify as Democrats and 72% of independent voters were in favor, while 66% of Republicans were opposed. When told such a single-payer model would eliminate private insurance plans, that overall support dropped to 52% — still well ahead of the 37% favorability seen in the 2020 survey. Medicare is the US government program that provides health coverage to about 70 million people aged 65 and older or with disabilities. Lawmakers, including US Senator Bernie Sanders, an Independent from Vermont, have suggested expanding Medicare to ensure health coverage that currently relies heavily on employers. Most developed countries have a single-payer system. The poll also found broad bipartisan support for a complete redesign of the US healthcare system at a time of economic uncertainty for many voters. "All year, KFF polls have shown that the public is frustrated with the high cost of healthcare, and that may be leading to a desire for change," said Audrey Kearney, a senior survey analyst at KFF. LEADING ECONOMIC CONCERN Healthcare expenses were the leading economic concern for Americans surveyed, with 60% of respondents saying they are very or somewhat worried about affording health costs. Gasoline and grocery costs followed at 59% and 52%, respectively. KFF's survey, conducted in September, includes responses from 1,328 US adults, the vast majority of them registered voters. Several progressive candidates this year in states that could help determine the congressional balance of power have come out in favor of a government-run health insurance system. Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic US Senate candidate from Michigan, has argued that the change would lower costs and expand coverage. Ahead of the November 3 elections, more voters are eager to hear congressional candidates discuss health insurance access, KFF said. Some 30 million of the 340 million US residents will be uninsured this year, up from 26.6 million in 2025, according to estimates from the [USN:L1N3IG0PA TEXT:"Congressional Budget Office"], as federal funding declines for Affordable Care Act plans and for Medicaid for low-income people. Private companies, such as CVS Health (CVS.N) , UnitedHealth (UNH.N) and Humana (HUM.N) , operate health plans for employers as well as Medicare and Medicaid plans. Asked about Medicare for all if it led to delays in tests and treatments, higher taxes and damage to the current Medicare program, as some opponents claim, Kearney said support fell. It rises, however, when they are told such a system would make health insurance a right and could eliminate premiums and cost-sharing. "These are the types of claims opponents and proponents would likely make in any real debate," Kearney said.

item.title: Burnham se plantea retrasar el aumento del gasto en defensa británico, según The Times
item.description: El primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham, está barajando la posibilidad de retrasar el anuncio sobre cómo y cuándo Reino Unido aumentará el gasto en defensa hasta el 3% del PIB, informó el martes el diario The Times, lo que pospondría un hito clave en el camino hacia el cumplimiento del objetivo de la OTAN del 3,5% para 2035.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham, está barajando la posibilidad de retrasar el anuncio sobre cómo y cuándo Reino Unido aumentará el gasto en defensa hasta el 3% del PIB, informó el martes el diario The Times, lo que pospondría un hito clave en el camino hacia el cumplimiento del objetivo de la OTAN del 3,5% para 2035. Reino Unido se ha visto presionado para detallar cómo cumplirá el compromiso con la OTAN y cómo responderá a una amenaza para la seguridad cada vez mayor. Burnham se ha comprometido a cumplir el objetivo de 2035, pero su Gobierno aún no ha detallado las medidas necesarias para lograrlo. El ministro de Hacienda, John Healey, dijo a principios de este año que esbozaría una hoja de ruta inicial para alcanzar el 3% del PIB en la próxima revisión del gasto, prevista para la primavera boreal de 2027. The Times citó a una fuente que afirmaba que la "hipótesis de trabajo" era que la revisión tendría lugar en octubre de 2027. Un portavoz del Ministerio de Hacienda dijo que era erróneo hablar de un retraso. "La fecha de la revisión del gasto aún no se ha fijado. Se trata de meros rumores y especulaciones", dijo el portavoz en un correo electrónico. Poniendo de relieve los retos de seguridad a los que se enfrenta Reino Unido, Estados Unidos retiró el domingo sus bombarderos de una base aérea en Inglaterra después de que esta fuera objeto de un presunto complot iraní. Los ministros han pospuesto en repetidas ocasiones las decisiones sobre la financiación adicional para defensa durante los últimos dos años. Healey, ministro de Hacienda desde julio, dimitió como ministro de Defensa en el Gobierno anterior tras no conseguir la financiación necesaria para elevar el gasto en defensa al 3% del PIB para 2030, una medida que contribuyó a la caída del entonces primer ministro Keir Starmer. Según la Oficina de Responsabilidad Presupuestaria, alcanzar ese objetivo intermedio le costaría al Gobierno 17.300 millones de libras esterlinas (22.900 millones de dólares) adicionales. Para cubrir las necesidades del actual Plan de Inversión en Defensa, Healey debe subsanar un déficit de financiación de 4.700 millones de libras esterlinas. Healey tiene previsto presentar su primer presupuesto el 28 de octubre. (1 dólar = 0,7559 libras)

item.title: World Bank raises Africa's 2026 growth forecast, urges AI investments
item.description: The World Bank has raised Africa's 2026 economic growth forecast to 4.3%, citing stronger performance across the region, and urged governments to embrace artificial intelligence to boost productivity and create jobs.
item.dc:creator: Duncan Miriri
item.content:encoded: The World Bank has raised Africa's 2026 economic growth forecast to 4.3%, citing stronger performance across the region, and urged governments to embrace artificial intelligence to boost productivity and create jobs. The region has weathered a tough global environment, the lender said in its Africa Economic Update report on Tuesday, marked by higher energy prices due to the impact of the Iran war on supply chains. The new growth forecast is up from the 4.1% expected in April. In 2025, the region's economy grew by 4.1%. The upgrade shows growing confidence that reforms in some of Africa's biggest economies are paying off even as the Iran war roils global energy markets. But these gains have yet to make a dent in poverty, with per capita income growth still trailing broader economic growth across much of the continent. "Economic activity in Sub-Saharan Africa continues to demonstrate remarkable resilience, with growth forecasts upgraded for nearly three-quarters of countries in the region," said Andrew Dabalen, the World Bank's chief economist for Africa. Zambia, Nigeria, Ethiopia and Angola all saw an upgrade to their growth forecast, the bank said, attributing gains to years of economic reforms and better economic management starting to pay off. Risks remained, however, including a prolonged Middle East conflict, the El Niño weather phenomenon, high interest rates in advanced economies and elevated debt servicing costs, Dabalen said. National debt loads in the region have stabilised with the debt-to-GDP ratio at about 57%, the World Bank report said, but about half of the countries are either in default or struggling to service their debts, pointing to persistently high debt service costs. INVESTMENTS IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE Faster growth is not translating into significant poverty reduction, the World Bank warned, with per capita income growth expected to increase only to 1.8% this year from 1.6% last year. "The next challenge is turning growth into more jobs and better opportunities," Dabalen said. He urged governments to focus on AI investments to boost economic growth rates, pointing to massive investments in countries such as the US that lift global growth. While Africa lacks the infrastructure and capital to compete with larger economies on AI, it can still benefit from practical, low-cost applications on affordable devices, Dabalen said. Examples include AI tools that support student learning, help farmers detect and manage livestock diseases, and automate tasks such as accounting for small businesses, he said. Shared data centres and stronger data protection laws could help accelerate AI adoption, he added.

item.title: España prevé aprobar los decretos sobre vivienda que provocaron las elecciones anticipadas
item.description: El Gobierno español tiene previsto aprobar este martes dos decretos sobre vivienda cuyo rechazo por parte de la Cámara Baja del Parlamento la semana pasada llevó al presidente Pedro Sánchez a convocar elecciones anticipadas, dijo el ministro de Cultura, Ernest Urtasun.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno español tiene previsto aprobar este martes dos decretos sobre vivienda [USN:L6N45O0VE TEXT:"cuyo rechazo"] por parte de la Cámara Baja del Parlamento la semana pasada llevó al presidente Pedro Sánchez a convocar [USN:L6N45R0A1 TEXT:"elecciones anticipadas"], dijo el ministro de Cultura, Ernest Urtasun. A continuación, los decretos se remitirán para su aprobación a la Diputación Permanente, un grupo reducido de diputados en funciones que permanecen en sus cargos tras la disolución del Parlamento de cara a las elecciones del 29 de noviembre, según informó la cadena pública TVE. El grupo de 69 diputados, entre los que se incluye a la presidenta del Congreso de los Diputados, Francina Armengol, del Partido Socialista Obrero Español (PSOE), que lidera Sánchez, cuenta con una escasa mayoría a favor de las medidas, que incluyen topes a los alquileres, una prohibición temporal de los desahucios y límites a la compra de viviendas por parte de empresas, según la cadena estatal TVE. Los decretos se aplicarían de forma temporal hasta que se constituya un nuevo Parlamento, según TVE. Urtasun declaró el lunes a los periodistas que los decretos presentarían algunas pequeñas variaciones, pero ningún cambio sustancial en comparación con los aprobados por el Consejo de Ministros y rechazados por el Parlamento la semana pasada. "Los decretos no se pueden presentar exactamente igual a como estaban la última vez, pero sí que les puedo garantizar que en ningún caso esas variaciones van a suponer la rebaja de ninguna de las medidas de protección que acordamos, ninguna", dijo Urtasun. Sánchez, que ofrecerá una rueda de prensa tras la reunión del Consejo de Ministros, dijo el lunes que necesitaba más escaños en el Parlamento tras no haber conseguido el apoyo suficiente para sus propuestas destinadas a abordar [USN:L6N45S0B3 TEXT:"la crisis"] de la vivienda, que ha provocado protestas en todo el país tras [USN:L6N45F0OT TEXT:"el intento"] de desahucio de una mujer de 87 años en Madrid.

item.title: Bain, GIC explore IPO or sale of Japan's WHI at valuation of about $3.2 billion, sources say
item.description: Bain Capital and Singapore's GIC are exploring prospects for an IPO or sale for Japan's WHI Holdings at a valuation of at least 500 billion yen ($3.2 billion) for the human resources software company, two people with knowledge of the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Miho Uranaka, Yantoultra Ngui
item.content:encoded: Bain Capital and Singapore's GIC are exploring prospects for an IPO or sale for Japan's WHI Holdings at a valuation of at least 500 billion yen ($3.2 billion) for the human resources software company, two people with knowledge of the matter said. The US private investment firm and Singapore sovereign wealth fund, which jointly control WHI, have begun sounding out advisers, potential buyers and investors in the process, the sources said. A listing in Japan is one option being considered, in addition to a sale to a strategic buyer or another financial investor, added the people, who sought anonymity as the matter is private. The talks are at an early stage and no final decision has been made, they added, while Bain and GIC could still decide to retain ownership. Bain and GIC declined to comment. There was no immediate comment from WHI. Bain set up WHI in 2019 through the carve-out and acquisition of the human resources software business of Works Applications, according to Bain's website. [USN:T9N35P01S TEXT:"In March 2023"] GIC agreed to invest alongside Bain and the two firms became co-control shareholders, the companies said in announcements. WHI's main operating company, Works Human Intelligence, develops and sells a human resources system used by about 1,200 large corporate groups for payroll, employee data, attendance and talent management, its website says. ($1=157.9400 yen)

item.title: Litauen ebnet Weg für Atomwaffen und wirbt um US-Stützpunkt
item.description: Litauen hat den Weg für eine Aufhebung des Atomwaffenverbots auf seinem Territorium geebnet und zugleich die Übernahme aller Kosten für einen dauerhaften US-Militärstützpunkt angeboten. Bei der ersten von zwei notwendigen Abstimmungen sprachen sich am Dienstag 106 der 141 Abgeordneten im Parlament für eine entsprechende Verfassungsänderung aus. Das baltische Land, das an die russische Exklave Kaliningrad und den russischen Verbündeten Belarus grenzt, ist Mitglied der EU und der Nato. Die Gesetzesänderung soll Verbote aufheben, die vor mehr als drei Jahrzehnten nach der Abspaltung Litauens von der Sowjetunion eingeführt wurden. Der russische Präsident Wladimir Putin hatte am Montag für den Fall einer Bedrohung von Kaliningrad mit dem Einsatz des gesamten militärischen Arsenals gedroht und damit die Spannungen in der Region erhöht.

item.content:encoded: Litauen hat den Weg für eine Aufhebung des Atomwaffenverbots auf seinem Territorium geebnet und zugleich die Übernahme aller Kosten für einen dauerhaften US-Militärstützpunkt angeboten. Bei der ersten von zwei notwendigen Abstimmungen sprachen sich am Dienstag 106 der 141 Abgeordneten im Parlament für eine entsprechende Verfassungsänderung aus. Das baltische Land, das an die russische Exklave Kaliningrad und den russischen Verbündeten Belarus grenzt, ist Mitglied der EU und der Nato. Die Gesetzesänderung soll Verbote aufheben, die vor mehr als drei Jahrzehnten nach der Abspaltung Litauens von der Sowjetunion eingeführt wurden. Der russische Präsident Wladimir Putin hatte am Montag für den Fall einer Bedrohung von Kaliningrad mit dem Einsatz des gesamten militärischen Arsenals [USN:L8N45N1KI TEXT:"gedroht"] und damit die Spannungen in der Region erhöht. Die Reform in Litauen benötigt für ihr Inkrafttreten eine Zweidrittelmehrheit in beiden Parlamentsabstimmungen. Der zweite Wahlgang ist für den 12. Januar geplant. Präsident Gitanas Nauseda hatte im Juli erklärt, die politischen Parteien hätten sich auf diesen Schritt geeinigt. Ihm zufolge gibt es keine unmittelbaren Pläne, Atomwaffen in Litauen zu lagern. Die Aufhebung des Verbots erlaube es dem Land jedoch, bei einer veränderten Sicherheitslage zu handeln. Litauen werde zudem Vertragspartei des Atomwaffensperrvertrags bleiben, sagte der Präsident. Zudem erklärte Ministerpräsident Mindaugas Sinkevicius am Dienstag, Litauen sei bereit, die Kosten für die Einrichtung eines dauerhaften US-Militärstützpunkts zu tragen. US-Präsident Donald Trump hatte am Montag erklärt, er werde den litauischen Antrag prüfen. "Sie sind Freunde von mir, sie sind großartige Menschen, also werden wir uns das sicherlich ansehen", sagte Trump. Die USA haben seit 2019 ein Panzerbataillon mit fast 1000 Soldaten in Litauen stationiert, die im Rahmen von Rotationen alle paar Monate ausgetauscht werden. Sinkevicius hatte im September bei einem Treffen mit Trumps Gesandtem John Coale in Vilnius vorgeschlagen, diese Präsenz in eine dauerhafte Stationierung umzuwandeln. Dies sei eine entscheidende Garantie für Abschreckung und Sicherheit, erklärte der Ministerpräsident. "Unsere Partner müssen lediglich die politische Entscheidung treffen, Truppen dauerhaft zu stationieren", fügte er hinzu. Litauen sei bereit, die damit verbundenen Kosten zu übernehmen.

item.title: How Trump's America First policy hit the Ebola response in Congo
item.description: When US doctor Patrick LaRochelle realized in May that he'd been exposed to Ebola in a mining town in Democratic Republic of Congo, he expected to be rushed home for treatment.
item.dc:creator: Yasmeen Abutaleb, Simon Lewis, Ammu Kannampilly, Emma Farge
item.content:encoded: When US doctor Patrick LaRochelle realized in May that he'd been exposed to Ebola in a mining town in Democratic Republic of Congo, he expected to be rushed home for treatment. That's what happened to him during a previous outbreak in 2018. And this time, at least three of the 13 state-of-the-art US biocontainment centers had agreed to treat him and his infected US colleague Peter Stafford. Then the plan changed. According to a senior administration official, once the White House heard US citizens had been exposed to the deadly virus in Congo, it delivered a clear directive: None would be coming home for treatment. The decision to pull down the shutters flew in the face of years of investment and preparation and set the tone for a US Ebola response focused more on border controls than fighting the disease, according to more than 50 people including current and former senior administration officials, US doctors and nurses, people involved in this outbreak and previous ones, as well as public health and legal experts. President Donald Trump's administration instead set up a 50-bed Ebola quarantine camp for US citizens on an air force base in Kenya and doubled-down on its closed-doors policy in July with a [USN:L6N43G03S TEXT:""do-not-board" order"] blocking citizens from taking US-bound flights if they had been anywhere in Congo within 21 days. The fallout from the administration's America First closed-borders philosophy is now playing out in an Ebola outbreak that's spreading at the [USN:L6N4230VL TEXT:"fastest rate ever"] and has killed more than [USN:S8N3XH0CZ TEXT:"4,000 people"]. The threat of offshore treatment for exposed citizens and the 21-day policy have dramatically slowed the flow of American medical volunteers, increasing the strain on local doctors and weakening the overall response, 19 of the people said. Trump's shutdown of the US Agency for International Development (USAID) and withdrawal from the WHO also left a [USN:L6N42H0NQ TEXT:"hole in the supply chain"] for medicines and equipment and disrupted medical work in a country almost six times the size of California. Medical missionary LaRochelle was transported to an isolation unit in Prague in the Czech Republic. He didn't contract the disease. Stafford went to Germany for treatment, and recovered. Both doctors said they were grateful for the US government's help and praised their care, but were sad they weren't flown home. "It seems like so much is motivated by fear and by the optics, rather than a true understanding of medical risk," LaRochelle told Reuters. "It felt like decisions were patched together and reactive," said the 46-year-old doctor, who has lived in Congo for 11 years with his wife, a family nurse practitioner, and their three children. "It makes me sad that we're at that point, and there are times that I feel angry." Stafford said his evacuation was delayed several times for logistical reasons and when he heard he was going to Germany, he assumed it would be to a US military hospital. Instead, he went to Berlin's Charite hospital. "I was disappointed and certainly sad that my home country was kind of rejecting us," Stafford told Reuters. "I would have loved to get treated in the US." QUARANTINE CHALLENGE Traditionally, the US played a key leadership role during Ebola epidemics, alongside the affected countries, the World Health Organization and - since its inception in 2016 - the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention. The US Department of Health and Human Services helped track and treat the disease wherever it spread, spending heavily to develop vaccines fast and bringing sick Americans home for treatment. This time, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. – a longtime anti-vaccine activist – has taken little interest and deployed relatively few resources from his sprawling $1.8 trillion agency to accelerate vaccine development for the Bundibugyo virus, a rare Ebola species. Instead, the US State Department chipped in $50 million to the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, a global partnership set up in 2016 to help develop shots for pandemics and epidemics. CEPI has allocated $100 million to fund Bundibugyo vaccine research but needs another $128 million for a large-scale trial in Congo, a spokesperson said. Since taking office last year, Kennedy has minimized the importance of fighting infectious diseases, despite a historic [USN:L2N3PH1HA TEXT:"measles"] outbreak. He has [USN:L3N3QA0ZS TEXT:"fired thousands"] at the US CDC, the Food and Drug Administration, and the National Institutes of Health, including disease and vaccine experts, and is focused on initiatives questioning the safety of [USN:L8N3Y61FI TEXT:"vaccinations"]. "This characterization of the US Ebola response overlooks the extensive work HHS and CDC are leading both at home and in Africa," Health Department spokeswoman Emily Hilliard said in a statement. "Protecting Americans from importation and combating the outbreak at its source are both essential parts of our response." In June, the health agency [USN:L4N42H17U TEXT:"sent doses"] of an experimental drug to the region for use in clinical trials. Kennedy didn't receive a formal briefing on the current outbreak for weeks after it was detected in May, two people familiar with his schedule said. Hilliard said Kennedy has received regular briefings from agency experts, including the CDC, and is deeply engaged in the US response. Kennedy's conspicuous absence during the second worst Ebola outbreak on record left a vacuum filled in part by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and at the outset by top White House official Stephen Miller and his team, who pushed the closed-borders strategy aggressively behind the scenes. Public health officials say stopping Ebola entering the US is a legitimate goal but the 21-day quarantine policy is having a tangible impact on staffing, and morale. "This is something that has been difficult and discouraging for these medical workers. They have traveled around the world to fight Ebola and they should be treated as heroes," said Franklin Graham, President and CEO of US faith-based aid organization Samaritan's Purse. Graham told Reuters that Americans once made up 80% of staff at the charity's Ebola Treatment Centers in Congo. Now it's about 20%. He said the cost of deploying medical professionals, who typically go for month-long stints, had more than doubled because of the quarantine policy. "The most effective way to respond to an Ebola outbreak is to safely bring as many highly trained medical professionals as you can to the epicenter, but these quarantine requirements are making that a real challenge," Graham said. The US facility in Kenya, built for an estimated $70 million, is currently empty and has only [USN:L6N43J0DT TEXT:"housed seven people"]. Its tents and converted shipping containers, Starlink Wi-Fi, air conditioning, catering services, along with more than 100 staff, all stand ready to welcome US citizens, a US official said. item.title: Wall Street profits soar to $45.9 billion in first half of 2026, report shows
item.description: Profits for the US securities industry totaled $45.9 billion in the first half of the year, putting it on track for a new annual record, according to a report released on Tuesday by New York State Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Profits for the US securities industry totaled $45.9 billion in the first half of the year, putting it on track for a new annual record, according to a report released on Tuesday by New York State Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli. A revival in dealmaking, strong trading revenue fueled by market volatility, resilient loan growth and a resurgent IPO market have boosted [USN:L6N43F12X TEXT:"nearly every major"] Wall Street business this year. Here are more details: Securities profits soared to a record $65.1 billion in 2025, up more than 30% from the prior year, the report showed Profits in the first half of 2026 surged 51.3% from a year ago If they keep up the same pace, profits could exceed $90 billion for 2026 "This figure would also outpace even inflation-adjusted record levels in 2009," the report said Wall Street remains a crucial pillar of New York City's economy, supporting hundreds of thousands of jobs and generating billions of dollars in tax revenue each year The report said the industry contributed at least $7.8 billion to the city's budget in fiscal year 2026, up 15.8% from a year ago

item.title: Zambia to sign $1.5 billion US health pact after resolving differences over data-sharing
item.description: Zambia's government will sign an agreement allowing it to receive $1.5 billion in health funding from the United States after resolving concerns over Washington's request for medical data, its health minister said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Zambia's government will sign an agreement allowing it to receive $1.5 billion in health funding from the United States after resolving concerns over Washington's request for medical data, its health minister said on Tuesday. Earlier this year [USN:L8N41H0XF TEXT:"negotiations stalled"] over Zambia's concerns over data privacy and a US attempt to tie the funding to access to critical minerals. Below are more comments by Health Minister Roma Chilengi at a press conference: "The government is pleased to announce that it will sign the agreement ... on Thursday," Chilengi said The minister said the agreement would see the US provide $1.5 billion in health funding over five years, while Zambia would spend $2.1 billion The US is a major funder of HIV/AIDS, malaria and public health programmes in the Southern African copper-producing nation Zambia and other African nations have had reservations over requests that they share sweeping medical data with the US as a condition to receive funds Chilengi said data-sharing would be limited to providing information required to monitor and evaluate US-funded health programmes. A clause had been removed that would have required Zambia to share patient medical specimens with the US if requested On whether the US funding was conditional on mining access, he said "there is no mention of critical minerals" in the health pact Chilengi said he was also not aware of a separate critical minerals agreement being negotiated with the US African countries including Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda have signed similar US health pacts, which are part of the Trump administration's changed approach to foreign aid under which poorer countries are meant to transition from aid to self-reliance. item.title: Ue, esportatori avranno un anno in più per adeguarsi a norme su metano - Von der Leyen
item.description: Agli esportatori di metano verrà concesso un anno in più per prepararsi al regolamento dell’Unione europea sul metano, ha affermato la presidente della Commissione Ursula von der Leyen, ribadendo che l’Europa sta affrontando pressioni dovute agli elevati costi energetici.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Agli esportatori di metano verrà concesso un anno in più per prepararsi al regolamento dell’Unione europea sul metano, ha affermato la presidente della Commissione Ursula von der Leyen, ribadendo che l’Europa sta affrontando pressioni dovute agli elevati costi energetici. "Concederemo agli esportatori un anno in più di flessibilità per quanto riguarda il metano", ha detto von der Leyen al Parlamento europeo. Ha aggiunto che la Commissione europea avvierà un dialogo strategico sulle raffinerie europee, con l’obiettivo di ridurre i costi, e che nei prossimi mesi Bruxelles proporrà misure per aumentare la quota di elettricità nel fabbisogno energetico complessivo. "Stiamo tutti risentendo di questi costi più elevati. Le imprese sono sottoposte a forte pressione. I cittadini fanno fatica a pagare le bollette. E la situazione potrebbe aggravarsi con l’avvicinarsi dell’inverno. Dobbiamo quindi agire subito", ha affermato von der Leyen.

item.content:encoded: L'azionario europeo sfiora i massimi di una settimana, con Genmab in testa ai rialzi nel comparto healthcare, mentre i rendimenti dei titoli di Stato della zona euro arretrano dopo il rialzo innescato dai timori fiscali e inflazionistici. ** Intorno alle 10.00 l’indice paneuropeo Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) guadagna lo 0,8% a 638,39 punti, avviandosi verso la terza seduta consecutiva di rialzi. ** GENMAB (GMAB.CO) balza dell'8,3%, posizionandosi in testa allo Stoxx 600 dopo che la combinazione di farmaci contro il tumore del sangue sviluppata dalla società biotech danese e dalla casa farmaceutica statunitense AbbVie (ABBV.N) ha dimostrato di ridurre il rischio di progressione della malattia o di decesso, in uno studio in fase avanzata. ** Il comparto healthcare nel suo complesso (.SXDP) sale dell’1,5%. ** L’attenzione si sposta ora sui dati relativi alle vendite al dettaglio della zona euro e sull’indagine Pmi di S&P Global per il Regno Unito, attesi in giornata, che potrebbero fornire indicazioni sulla spesa dei consumatori nella regione e sull’attività economica britannica. ** L’euro oscilla vicino ai minimi degli ultimi 17 mesi, appesantito dall’incertezza politica dopo che ieri il primo ministro spagnolo Pedro Sanchez ha indetto elezioni anticipate. ** Nel frattempo, il governo di Parigi sta cercando di approvare un'impopolare manovra di bilancio per il 2027 volta a ridurre il deficit, scatenando una fuga dai titoli di Stato francesi. ** Ciononostante, i rendimenti dei titoli di Stato della zona euro arretrano, dopo aver toccato la scorsa settimana i massimi degli ultimi decenni. ** Tra i singoli titoli, l’italiana TECHNOPROBE (TPRO.MI) avanza del 3,6% dopo che J.P. Morgan ha avviato la copertura del titolo con un rating 'overweight'.

item.content:encoded: L’euro si attesta appena sopra il minimo degli ultimi 17 mesi, mentre i mercati obbligazionari della zona euro si stabilizzano, all’indomani del brusco calo della valuta causato dai timori che le tensioni sui titoli di Stato francesi potessero estendersi su scala più ampia. ** L'euro cede meno dello 0,1% a 1,12 dollari, dopo essere sceso ieri ai minimi da maggio 2025 a 1,116 dollari, ampliando così il calo di oltre l'1% registrato la scorsa settimana. ** La moneta unica è sotto pressione a causa dei timori relativi agli elevati livelli di indebitamento e allo stallo politico in Francia, con le imminenti elezioni anticipate in Spagna che aggravano ulteriormente la situazione. ** Nel mercato più ampio il dollaro rimane forte, sostenuto dai rendimenti dei Treasury ancora elevati, che ieri hanno toccato i massimi degli ultimi decenni. L’indice del dollaro è sostanzialmente invariato a 102,008, dopo aver raggiunto ieri il massimo degli ultimi 18 mesi a 102,53. ** La forza del biglietto verde si manifesta nonostante le ridotte aspettative di un rialzo dei tassi da parte della Federal Reserve questo mese, sulla scia di dati sull’occupazione statunitense inferiori alle attese, poiché gli investitori scommettono che la banca centrale dovrà comunque inasprire ulteriormente la politica monetaria. Secondo Cme FedWatch, la probabilità di un rialzo a ottobre è del 22%, mentre sale a circa l’85% per dicembre. ** Rispetto allo yen, il dollaro guadagna lo 0,2% a 158,14 , mentre la sterlina rimane pressoché invariata a 1,323 dollari.

item.title: Bce, rendimenti elevati freneranno trasferimento prezzi energia - Rehn
item.description: La rapida inflazione nel settore energetico in tutta la zona euro non si è ancora estesa ad altri beni e servizi, e il recente aumento dei rendimenti dei titoli di Stato dovrebbe attenuare le pressioni sui prezzi, frenando al contempo la crescita.

item.content:encoded: La rapida inflazione nel settore energetico in tutta la zona euro non si è ancora estesa ad altri beni e servizi, e il recente aumento dei rendimenti dei titoli di Stato dovrebbe attenuare le pressioni sui prezzi, frenando al contempo la crescita. Lo ha detto oggi Olli Rehn, membro del Consiglio direttivo della Banca centrale europea. Sebbene numerosi responsabili della politica monetaria abbiano affermato che i rischi inflazionistici sono orientati verso valori più elevati del previsto, Rehn ha sottolineato che vi sono anche altri fattori da considerare, poiché nell’economia sono all’opera forze contrapposte. "Il rialzo dei tassi di interesse a lungo termine contribuisce a rallentare la crescita e anche a ridurre il trasferimento dei prezzi dell’energia sui prezzi dei beni non energetici e sui salari", ha detto Rehn, facendo eco ad alcune osservazioni del capo economista della Bce Philip Lane.

Lo ha detto Philip Lane, capo economista della Banca centrale europea, all’agenzia stampa Ansa. "Quanto agli effetti second-round, finora non ne abbiamo osservati di molto intensi. Continuiamo a monitorarli", ha affermato Lane in un’intervista pubblicata oggi. "Per questo, pur essendo io un promotore degli scenari, è troppo semplicistico dire che ci troviamo nello scenario avverso o in quello di riferimento". "I prezzi dell’energia sono elevati, ma l’intensità della trasmissione al resto dell’economia resta incerta", ha aggiunto Lane.

item.title: ANALISI Timori di contagio da bond Francia mettono a dura prova euro
item.description: Il calo dell’euro rappresenta l’ultimo campanello d’allarme per i banchieri centrali, che devono affrontare uun vero e proprio rally dei costi di indebitamento francesi che ha iniziato a ripercuotersi sull’intera area dell’euro.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Il calo dell’euro rappresenta l’ultimo campanello d’allarme per i banchieri centrali, che devono affrontare uun vero e proprio rally dei costi di indebitamento francesi che ha iniziato a ripercuotersi sull’intera area dell’euro. Ieri la divisa unica ha toccato i minimi degli ultimi 17 mesi, scendendo sotto quota 1,12 dollari , e ha registrato un crollo rispetto alla sterlina , al franco svizzero e allo yen . Parigi è al centro delle preoccupazioni dei mercati europei. Il governo francese sta cercando di approvare un impopolare bilancio per il 2027 volto a ridurre il deficit e a contenere il debito pubblico, che ha raggiunto livelli record: un compito arduo in un parlamento profondamente diviso, mentre i partiti guardano alle elezioni presidenziali del prossimo anno. Gli investitori, restii a correre rischi, stanno vendendo in massa i titoli di Stato francesi per acquistare invece quelli tedeschi, considerati più sicuri. Con il premio richiesto dagli investitori per detenere titoli di Stato francesi anziché tedeschi al livello più alto dalla crisi del debito della zona euro del 2012, i mercati valutari ora temono un effetto contagio. La posta in gioco è una crscita debole in un blocco scosso dall’incertezza politica. Il mese scorso il partito del cancelliere Friedrich Merz ha subito la peggiore sconfitta elettorale regionale nella Germania del dopoguerra. E ieri il primo ministro spagnolo Pedro Sanchez ha indetto elezioni anticipate. Anche l’Italia terrà le elezioni l’anno prossimo. Con l’inflazione già in aumento a causa dell’impennata dei costi energetici e dei rendimenti più elevati che fanno lievitare i costi di indebitamento per famiglie e imprese, un ulteriore indebolimento dell’euro potrebbe mettere la Banca centrale europea in una situazione di stallo tra la lotta all’inflazione e la necessità di calmare i mercati obbligazionari. Il differenziale tra i rendimenti dei titoli di Stato francesi e tedeschi a 10 anni ha registrato la scorsa settimana il più forte balzo settimanale degli ultimi decenni, mentre il differenziale tra i rendimenti italiani e tedeschi ha toccato quasi 130 punti base, segnando il più forte aumento su base settimanale dalla crisi del Covid. "Il sell-off dei titoli obbligazionari sta provocando movimenti più marcati su tutto ciò che viene percepito come più vulnerabile e ciò ha innescato un’ondata di vendite dell’euro", ha detto Kit Juckes, responsabile strategia valutaria di Société Générale. "Credo che i fattori che hanno mantenuto il cambio euro/dollaro al di sopra dei livelli chiave durante l’estate… siano ormai scomparsi", ha aggiunto, riferendosi alle precedenti ipotesi di uno shock energetico di breve durata e di una strategia Usa volta a indebolire il dollaro. UNA NUOVA DIMENSIONE DELLA DEBOLEZZA DELL’EURO Sebbene l’euro si trovi ben al di sopra dei minimi degli ultimi 20 anni toccati nel 2022, quando l’invasione russa dell’Ucraina ha scatenato una crisi energetica, i movimenti del mercato obbligazionario aggiungono una nuova dimensione alla debolezza dell’euro. Ogni ulteriore ampliamento di 10 punti base dello spread francese rispetto a quello tedesco comporterebbe un calo dello 0,4% del cambio euro/dollaro, secondo le stime degli strategist valutari di BofA. "La reazione tipica è per lo più vicina allo zero, ma (l’impatto dello spread) può aumentare significativamente in periodi di forte tensione", scrivono gli analisti di Goldman Sachs in una nota. "Gli spread non hanno importanza per la valuta finché non diventano l’unica cosa che conta", hanno aggiunto, sottolineando che l’impatto sull’euro aumenta quando un evento di rischio spinge al ribasso i rendimenti tedeschi, ma al rialzo quelli degli altri Paesi dell’Unione. È quanto è accaduto la scorsa settimana, quando il rendimento dei Bund tedeschi sono scesi di quasi 17 punti base, il calo settimanale più consistente dal 2024 . "Il cambio euro/dollaro è influenzato di solito soprattutto dal lato del dollaro, ma questa volta si registra un impatto anche dall’Europa", ha detto Andreas König di Amundi Asset Management. "Bisogna tornare un po’ indietro nel tempo per individuare l’ultima volta in cui le notizie europee hanno fatto muovere l’euro", ha aggiunto. König non intravede un'inversione di tendenza nel medio termine e mantiene una posizione 'overweight' sul dollaro, date le prospettive di crescita e di tassi negli Stati Uniti. I dati CFTC mostrano che gli operatori si sono posizionati in previsione di un calo dell’euro. I risk reversal a tre mesi sull’euro , che riflettono la differenza tra il costo di un’opzione di acquisto dell’euro e quello di un’opzione di vendita, sono scesi venerdì al livello più basso dal 2024. Gli analisti sostengono che l’euro potrebbe testare quota 1,10 dollari, mentre Juckes di SocGen sottolinea anche la vulnerabilità dell’euro rispetto a valute come lo yen e il franco svizzero. A settembre l’euro ha perso quasi il 4% rispetto allo yen. Il calo della valuta, unito alle tensioni sul mercato obbligazionario, ha spostato l’attenzione su come i banchieri centrali potrebbero stabilizzare i mercati, soprattutto se le elezioni francesi del 2027 dovessero causare ulteriori tensioni. Lo Strumento di protezione della trasmissione della Bce consente alla banca centrale di acquistare un numero illimitato di obbligazioni da un Paese che sta subendo un inasprimento "ingiustificato e disordinato" delle condizioni di finanziamento. Per ora, la crescita, sebbene debole, si è rafforzata. Secondo i dati di S&P Global, a settembre l’attività economica della zona euro ha registrato il ritmo di espansione più rapido degli ultimi quasi tre anni e mezzo. È inoltre al centro dell’attenzione la capacità delle banche, principali finanziatori delle imprese della regione, di continuare a erogare prestiti alle rispettive economie. "Se il rischio di contagio di bilancio in Europa non verrà arginato, prevedo un calo del cambio euro/dollaro", dice Stephen Jen, CEO e co-CIO di Eurizon SLJ Asset Management.

item.title: Indian insurance brokers oppose regulator's proposed reforms
item.description: Indian insurance brokers are opposing reform proposals from the country's regulator, including caps on commissions paid to banks, brokers, and agents, according to letters from the Insurance Brokers Association of India (IBAI) to the finance minister and prime minister, seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indian insurance brokers are opposing reform proposals from the country's regulator, including caps on commissions paid to banks, brokers, and agents, according to letters from the Insurance Brokers Association of India (IBAI) to the finance minister and prime minister, seen by Reuters. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India [USN:L6N45F0ZZ TEXT:"proposed the rules"] as part of a discussion paper in late September and invited stakeholders to submit feedback by October 25. Here are some details: The regulator's proposed rules include linking commission levels to the complexity of products and effort required to sell, with mandatory insurance covers such as third-party motor policies earning little or no commission. The reforms are aimed at reducing insurance costs for policyholders. However, the association said the proposed rules would shift money away from distributors and insurers' own employees to insurance company owners, without requiring any savings to be passed on to policyholders. The IBAI says in its letters that the new regulation may put at risk at least 1 million jobs over a five-year period, before counting salaried staff of insurers. It also argues that the reforms may lead to a resurgence of unethical practices, such as insurers disguising excess commissions as "marketing fees." A complete overhaul of distribution within months of allowing 100% foreign direct investment would signal high regulatory uncertainty, IBAI added. It urged the regulatory body to not enact hard caps on commissions without "published impact assessment covering policyholders, employment, public sector insurers and foreign investment". The IBAI has requested an audience with the finance minister and prime minister, asking that the current framework run till its scheduled 2028 review.

item.content:encoded: Die als Favoritin für die Präsidentschaftswahl im kommenden Jahr geltende Marine Le Pen will Frankreichs Staatsverschuldung drücken. Bis 2030 soll das Defizit auf drei Prozent fallen, kündigte die Kandidatin der rechtspopulistischen bis rechtsextremen Rassemblement National (RN) am Dienstag in Paris an. Frankreich könne seine finanzielle Unabhängigkeit verlieren, wenn nicht die "richtigen Entscheidungen" getroffen würden, sagte Le Pen auf einer Pressekonferenz. Sie kündigte an, während einer fünfjährigen Amtszeit Einsparungen von insgesamt 140 Milliarden Euro vornehmen zu wollen. Le Pen gilt Umfragen zufolge als Favoritin für die Präsidentschaftswahl im kommenden Frühjahr, bei der ein Nachfolger für den amtierenden Präsidenten Emmanuel Macron gesucht wird. Die jetzige Regierung geht für das laufende Jahr von einem öffentlichen Defizit von 5,4 Prozent aus. Die EU-Regeln sehen eigentlich eine Obergrenze von drei Prozent vor. An den Finanzmärkten ist Frankreich wegen seiner Haushaltsprobleme und eines schwächeren Wirtschaftswachstums zuletzt immer stärker in den Fokus geraten. Der Risikoaufschlag für französische gegenüber deutschen Staatsanleihen mit zehnjähriger Laufzeit hatte am Freitag mit 158 Basispunkten den höchsten Stand seit der Euro-Schuldenkrise vor 15 Jahren erreicht. "Frankreich hat noch nie ein konsequentes Bekenntnis zur Haushaltskonsolidierung gezeigt. Das muss jetzt aber geschehen", sagte Guillermo Felices, Anlagestratege bei PGIM. "Wer auch immer Frankreich führt, wird im Parlament einen Konsens für eine Haushaltskonsolidierung finden müssen, die über alles hinausgeht, was wir bisher von Frankreich gesehen haben." Die Industriestaaten-Organisation OECD geht davon aus, dass Frankreichs Schuldenberg in diesem Jahr auf fast 119 Prozent des Bruttoinlandsproduktes anschwellen wird. Für 2027 werden dann knapp 121 Prozent erwartet.

item.title: Sinner to miss rest of 2026 to recover from knee injury
item.description: World number one Jannik Sinner will not compete again in 2026 after opting to continue his recovery from a knee injury that has sidelined him since his triumphant Wimbledon campaign in July, the Italian said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: World number one Jannik Sinner will not compete again in 2026 after opting to continue his recovery from a knee injury that has sidelined him since his triumphant Wimbledon campaign in July, the Italian said on Tuesday. Sinner has not played since beating Alexander Zverev in the All England Club final on July 12, with the 25-year-old missing the North American hardcourt swing, the US Open as well as the ongoing slate of tournaments in Asia. He will now miss the European indoor hardcourt swing as well as the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin, where he won the title in the last two years. "Me, together with the doctors, have decided that I need a course of treatment for my knee which means the 2026 season is officially over," Sinner said in a video posted on X. "The last couple of years, especially the ending in Turin, gave me so many beautiful feelings and emotions which this year is going to be way different. "But at the moment, I also need to think about my long-term career. So I'll do everything possible to get back 100%." Sinner's team said in a statement that he would follow a course of treatment for inflammation in his knee. "The decision has been made to have the treatment now to give Jannik the necessary time to recover before beginning preparations for 2027," it added. Sinner's absence could open the door for Zverev to finish the year at the top of the world rankings. The German world number two has cut the gap to Sinner after winning the French Open and US Open titles.

item.title: Francia se prepara para un día de bloqueos en los institutos y manifestaciones callejeras
item.description: Francia se preparaba este martes para un día de bloqueos en institutos de todo el país y manifestaciones callejeras organizadas por los sindicatos en apoyo a los estudiantes, que exigen que el Gobierno del presidente Emmanuel Macron, con escasos recursos económicos, aborde el problema de la falta de personal y el deterioro de los centros educativos.
item.dc:creator: Inti Landauro
item.content:encoded: Francia se preparaba este martes para un día de bloqueos en institutos de todo el país y manifestaciones callejeras organizadas por los sindicatos en apoyo a los estudiantes, que exigen que el Gobierno del presidente Emmanuel Macron, con escasos recursos económicos, aborde el problema de la falta de personal y el deterioro de los centros educativos. Los estudiantes adolescentes se apostaron en barricadas formadas con contenedores de basura frente a los centros educativos, desde Lille, en el norte, hasta Marsella, en el sur, y desde Estrasburgo, en el este, hasta Nantes, en el oeste. En París, enarbolaron pancartas en las que se leía "Queremos que se nos escuche, no que nos lancen gases lacrimógenos" y "Nuestro futuro no es opcional". Las manifestaciones del martes se producen tras quince días de protestas que comenzaron en los barrios marginales de París antes de extenderse por todo el país. El Gobierno respondió con la policía antidisturbios, alegando que el movimiento se había transformado en violencia urbana. Un adolescente perdió una mano cuando los manifestantes de secundaria se enfrentaron con la policía antidisturbios en el norte de Francia el lunes. François-Xavier Lauch, prefecto de Pas-de-Calais, se negó a comentar las circunstancias exactas, señalando que entre 200 y 250 manifestantes habían estado lanzando objetos contra la policía. El periódico regional La Voix du Nord informó de que el joven de 15 años perdió la mano y parte del antebrazo tras recoger una granada de dispersión de la policía. EL PRIMER MINISTRO PROMETE UNA RESPUESTA El primer ministro, Sébastien Lecornu, ha ordenado a sus ministros que aborden las principales reivindicaciones de los estudiantes. Entre ellas se incluyen garantizar la sustitución de los profesores ausentes, revisar la duración de la jornada escolar —de 8:00 a 18:00 horas— y la necesidad de ampliar las pausas para comer. El Gobierno también estudiará las reparaciones necesarias en los edificios escolares, que se están quedando obsoletos, según dijo Lecornu, quien exigió a los ministros que presentaran sus primeras propuestas antes de finales de octubre. Pero encontrar fondos adicionales será difícil. Las protestas han aumentado la presión sobre un Gobierno que intenta reducir un déficit presupuestario cada vez mayor, mientras que la preocupación de los inversionistas por la creciente deuda de Francia, el débil crecimiento y la reticencia a frenar el gasto empujan al alza los rendimientos de los bonos. El rendimiento de los bonos franceses a 10 años alcanzó brevemente la semana pasada su máximo en 24 años, superando el 5%. El aumento de los costos de financiación de Francia ha comenzado a extenderse a toda la zona del euro, y la caída del euro es la última señal de alarma para los responsables de política monetaria. El ministro de Hacienda, Roland Lescure, dijo el martes que no era necesario que el Banco Central Europeo interviniera. MILES DE DETENCIONES El Ministerio de Justicia francés informó de que se ha detenido a 5.060 personas desde que comenzaron las protestas, de las cuales el 87% son menores de edad. Más de 1.800 personas están siendo procesadas, incluidos 1.483 menores, según el ministerio, que no especificó los delitos. Indicó que se habían desestimado 790 casos. Al menos 715 agentes de policía y 215 adolescentes han resultado heridos en los enfrentamientos, según la oficina de Lecornu. A seis meses de las elecciones para sustituir a Macron, su Gobierno y la formación de extrema derecha Agrupación Nacional, liderada por la favorita en las presidenciales, Marine Le Pen, han acusado a los diputados y alcaldes de la formación de izquierda Francia Insumisa (LFI, por sus siglas en francés) de avivar las protestas. LFI niega la acusación. Bally Bagayoko, alcalde de Saint-Denis —un suburbio pobre de París— y miembro de LFI, dijo que se oponía a la violencia, pero que apoyaba a los estudiantes que se manifestaban. "Me mantengo firme en mi postura de estar del lado de mis vecinos, y los estudiantes de secundaria son mis vecinos", dijo.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The underlying fundamentals of the oil and gas market are becoming tighter, Chevron (CVX.N) CEO Mike Wirth said on Tuesday, as the US-Israeli war with Iran continues into its eighth month and buffers for oil and fuel supply thin. The energy system is more fragile today than earlier in the conflict, while the oil price floor gets gradually higher, Wirth said at the Energy Intelligence Forum in London.

item.content:encoded: Die Bundesanwaltschaft hat den früheren Präsidenten des Bundesnachrichtendienstes (BND), August Hanning, und einen ehemaligen Mitarbeiter wegen des Verdachts der Spionage und des Landesverrats festnehmen lassen. Das teilte die Karlsruher Behörde am Dienstag mit. Die Festnahmen durch das Bundeskriminalamt erfolgten in Bayern und Nordrhein-Westfalen. Hanning wird unter anderem landesverräterische Ausspähung, versuchter Landesverrat und geheimdienstliche Agententätigkeit vorgeworfen. Sein mutmaßlicher Komplize Manfred D. soll Beihilfe geleistet haben. Hanning soll laut Bundesanwaltschaft über Jahre hinweg geheime BND-Dokumente von Manfred D. erhalten und für seine private Beratertätigkeit genutzt haben. Manfred D. war Hannings Büroleiter und hatte diese Funktion auch unter dessen Nachfolgern bis März 2026 inne. Demnach soll er Hanning bis Juni 2022 gegen Geld fast 2000 Dokumente zur Verfügung gestellt haben, darunter vielfach als Verschlusssache eingestufte Informationen für die Leitungsebene. In einem Fall soll Hanning die geheimen Informationen genutzt haben, um eine Analyse für den Mitarbeiter eines ausländischen Geheimdienstes zu erstellen. Zudem habe er über Jahre hinweg einen Angehörigen eines anderen staatlichen Nachrichtendienstes mit politischen Informationen versorgt. Die Ermittlungen kamen den Angaben zufolge ins Rollen, nachdem bei Hanning im September 2025 in einem anderen Verfahren der Staatsanwaltschaft Hamburg Beweismittel gefunden worden waren. Die beiden Beschuldigten sollen nun einem Ermittlungsrichter des Bundesgerichtshofs vorgeführt werden.

item.title: Spain, Portugal data centre boom spurs clean power, storage build
item.description: Power developers in Spain and Portugal must build day-and-night power solutions and clinch available grid points to capitalise on data centre builders lured by solar and wind.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Garcia
item.content:encoded: Abundant solar and wind resources and opportunities for grid connections have sparked a surge in data centre development in Spain and Portugal. The Iberian Peninsula will account for roughly 11.5% of installed data centre capacity in Europe by 2030, up from 5.8% in 2025, according to research group Rystad Energy. Spain's data centre capacity is forecast to rise fourfold in the next five years to reach 3.9 GW in 2030, enjoying the second largest increase in absolute terms in Europe, behind the UK. Neighbouring Portugal, which has a much smaller population, will grow faster than any other country to install over 1 GW of data centre capacity by the end of the decade, Rystad Energy predicts. Spain's capital Madrid and the northern regions of Aragon and Navarra will host the bulk of the announced pipeline, but other areas could become data centre hubs. High shares of intermittent solar and wind capacity in Spain and Portugal mean that power companies may need to invest in solutions that provide baseload or firm power supply, such as battery storage and hybrid plants, Odin Foldvik Eikeland Senior Analyst, Renewables & Power for EMEA at Rystad Energy, told Reuters Events. Renewable energy accounted for 56% of electricity generation in Spain in 2025 and over 80% in Portugal, official data from the European Commission shows. CHART: Cumulative installed capacity of data centres in Europe Source: Rystad Energy (2026) Other challenges for data centre developers in Iberia will include dwindling grid capacity in the coming years and environmental factors such as high temperatures and scarce water supplies. These headwinds will create "downside risk” for the capacity outlook, Eikeland said. Connecting in Spain Grid availability could determine where data centre developers locate facilities in Spain going forward. Roughly 70% of Spain's transmission nodes have no capacity available and data centre clusters around Madrid, Aragon – where Microsoft is investing 5.3 billion euros in three data centres – and Navarra, have little remaining headroom. Regions including Murcia, Andalucia, and Castilla y Leon show potential for grid connection availability, Eikeland said. For available grid capacity, “Spain still compares favorably with Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam or Dublin, but that gap is closing,” he noted. Equinix has six data centres in Madrid and two in Barcelona and has followed a strategy of placing its data centres inside strategic global metropolitan hubs to keep data physically close to users. “There is a lack of investments in substations, power lines, and infrastructure to bring the power generated hundreds of kilometers away from the points of consumption,” Valentín Pinuaga, Managing Director of Equinix Espana, told Reuters Events. The Spanish government last month authorized 17 billion euros ($19.6 billion) in investments in the power grid through 2030, some 30% more than initially planned. But transmission projects will take several years to materialize, in part due to ongoing supply chain bottlenecks for large power transformers, Pinagua said. Big Power As data centres prioritize access to grids and firm power supplies, large utilities such as Iberdrola, Endesa, and EDP are well positioned to capitalise. These companies are diversifying their generation portfolios away from solar in order to provide firmer power solutions, Eikeland said. Endesa is diversifying more into wind and battery storage. While Iberdrola and EDP have long-standing hydropower fleets that provide firm power, the recent rise in solar power generation means Iberdrola is diversifying into battery storage and more hydro, and EDP is developing hybrid and storage projects as well as repowering existing facilities, Eikeland said. Endesa plans 1.9 GW of new renewables by 2028, including 1.5 GW of wind plus batteries, as it seeks to move away from solar towards a more diversified generation profile. Download our exclusive report on Europe's shift to grid value technologies. Ana Quelhas, EVP Hydrogen and Data Centers at EDP Renewables, said that solar and wind will continue to play a central role in the company’s investment plans “because of the quality of the resource base and their competitiveness.” However, EDP plans to diversify its investments to maintain grid reliability and system adequacy. “That means future solutions will increasingly combine multiple technologies and capabilities, including renewable generation, storage, flexibility solutions and, where appropriate, other forms of firm capacity,” Quelhas told Reuters Events. Battery growth Battery storage will be key to ensuring the 24-hour operation of day centres. Merlin Properties, a leading data centre developer in Spain and Portugal, in February signed a 40-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with power developer Solaria for 426 MW of solar power and an additional 10-year contract for 600 MWh of battery energy storage. Solaria at the time described the deal as “the first hybrid solar and battery PPA signed in the Spanish market.” “Most important is that the region enables a strong buildout of batteries to help with the intermittent generation challenge and enables more large-scale hybrid PPA deals where the data centre developers can ensure more baseload power supply,” Eikeland said. For exclusive energy insights, sign up to our newsletter . Data centre developers must also factor in higher cooling costs and more water constraints in Spain and Portugal than in northern European countries, which has prompted many data centre developers to choose the chilly Nordic region over the Iberian Peninsula. Portugal builds Portugal has 36 operational data centres and a further 10 in construction or planning, according to Synertics, a Portuguese energy consultancy. The Lisbon area is the epicentre of the Portuguese data centre boom with nearly 1.4 GW planned, compared with just 25 MW of IT capacity currently operational. Although investments have so far been concentrated in the Lisbon and Porto metropolitan areas, “grid capacity in Portugal is more available than the market assumes,” and there are areas along existing transmission corridors that could attract data centre investments in the future, said Synertics CEO Manuel Pessanha. MAP: Data centres, high voltage transmission lines in Portugal Source: Synertics, 2026 A key project under development is Start Campus' 1.2 GW SINES data center campus in Sines, near Lisbon, currently scheduled to be completed in 2030. The facility is located at a decommissioned coal plant site and will use seawater for cooling. The first module has been up and running since early 2025 and now has 37 MW of computing capacity, much of which is provided to Microsoft through Nscale. A second 200 MW module that will come on stream in 2027 will also provide computing power to the Nscale-Microsoft collaboration, with four additional 200 MW modules slated to start operations over the next few years. Start Campus has not yet sold the additional capacity to data center developers but has a very strong pipeline from customers that want “two or more buildings,” Omer Wilson, Chief Marketing Officer of Start Campus, said. The developer has a PPA in place with EDP for the first module and a memorandum of understanding with the energy company “that allows us to look at a long roadmap of potential PPAs for the future,” Wilson said. “What we wanted to do with EDP was to look at how do can work with them on their new renewable projects to add capacity to the grid," he said. "So we will take from that added capacity in the coming years, not from the existing capacity for the population.” The partnership between Start Campus and EDP could lead to future data center projects elsewhere in Iberia. “EDP sits on a lot of solar plants and lots of different locations which could be very well suited for future data center development,” Wilson said. EDP is “actively engaging” with other data center developers and hyperscalers to build partnerships from the ground up, Quelhas said. “As projects grow larger, success depends less on negotiating a power contract at the end of the process and more on designing energy, infrastructure and demand solutions together from the beginning,” she said.

item.content:encoded: Europas Banken stehen nach Einschätzung des Chefs der Europäischen Bankenaufsichtsbehörde (EBA), Francois-Louis Michaud, trotz ihrer derzeit starken Ertragslage vor erheblichen Herausforderungen. Die Institute seien so profitabel wie lange nicht mehr, während die Kostenquoten gesunken seien, sagte Michaud am Dienstag bei einer Aufsichtskonferenz der österreichischen Finanzmarktaufsicht (FMA) in Wien. Das positive Bild dürfe jedoch nicht zu Selbstzufriedenheit führen. "Alles sieht gut aus", sagte Michaud mit Verweis auf gestiegene Gewinne und gesunkene Kosten. Die Banken hätten von den Reformen nach der Finanzkrise, einer verbesserten Risikosteuerung und dem Ausbau der europäischen Aufsichtsarchitektur profitiert. Zugleich warnte der EBA-Chef vor einem zunehmend unsicheren Umfeld. Hohe Staatsschulden, geopolitische Spannungen sowie mögliche Belastungen bei Kreditqualität und Betriebskosten könnten die Erträge künftig unter Druck setzen. Zudem seien die Bewertungen in einigen Marktsegmenten hoch, insbesondere im Zusammenhang mit dem Boom rund um Künstliche Intelligenz. Als weitere Herausforderungen nannte Michaud die Fragmentierung des europäischen Bankenmarktes sowie Cyberrisiken. Die EBA arbeite deshalb daran, Meldepflichten und regulatorische Vorgaben zu vereinfachen, um die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit der Banken zu stärken. Dabei gehe es nicht um geringere Kapitalanforderungen, sondern um einen effizienteren Regulierungsrahmen, betonte er.

item.title: Kenya confirms first Ebola case imported from Congo, patient has died
item.description: Kenya has recorded its first confirmed Ebola case, a Kenyan citizen who has been living in Democratic Republic of Congo and arrived in Nairobi on Saturday, health minister Aden Duale said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kenya has recorded its first confirmed Ebola case, a Kenyan citizen who has been living in Democratic Republic of Congo and arrived in Nairobi on Saturday, health minister Aden Duale said. The patient has since died, and 28 contacts have been identified so far including family members and health workers, Duale told a press conference. Congo has been battling its [USN:L8N43X0QI TEXT:"largest-ever"] Ebola outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo species. The outbreak was declared in mid-May but may have started months earlier and has so far resisted containment efforts, with the Central African country recording more than 8,000 cases and over [USN:L1N45O094 TEXT:"4,000 deaths"]. The outbreak earlier spread to Uganda, which reported 20 cases and two deaths, but the World Health Organization declared Uganda [USN:L6N44N0VL TEXT:"free of the disease"] in August. Ebola spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of infected people, living or dead. It can cause fever, vomiting, diarrhoea and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding.

item.title: UK construction activity falls at slowest pace since January
item.description: British construction activity fell further in September, but the decline was the smallest since January as a sharp downturn in housebuilding eased slightly, an industry survey showed on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: David Milliken
item.content:encoded: British construction activity fell further in September, but the decline was the smallest since January as a sharp downturn in housebuilding eased slightly, an industry survey showed on Tuesday. The S&P Global Purchasing Managers' Index for Britain's construction sector rose to an eight-month high of 46.1 in September from 44.3 in August but remained well below the 50 mark that divides growth from contraction, as it has been since January 2025. "Total new orders were relatively subdued in September as construction firms reported longer sales conversion cycles and clients deferred decision-making on major projects," Tim Moore, economics director at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said. The new orders balance fell to a three-month low of 45.9 from 47.7, due to a mix of subdued demand, geopolitical tensions and rising input costs Input prices rose at their slowest rate since the outbreak of the Iran war in February, but Moore said this appeared unlikely to last due to higher energy costs Firms' expectations for future activity were the weakest since May The most recent official data showed British construction output was 1.0% lower than a year earlier in Q2 2026 Housebuilding remained the weakest sector in the PMI, followed by civil engineering, while commercial work showed only a small decline S&P Global said their all-sector PMI, which includes PMI data for [USN:ZRN00EN1B TEXT:"services"], [USN:L8N45M1O7 TEXT:"manufacturing"] and construction, slipped to a three-month low of 51.5 in September from 51.8

item.title: Most Gulf markets gain as oil-supply worries ease, Fed hike bets recede
item.description: Most major Gulf stock markets opened higher on Tuesday, supported by easing concerns over oil supplies, reduced expectations of a near-term US interest rate hike and improving global risk sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Most major Gulf stock markets opened higher on Tuesday, supported by easing concerns over oil supplies, reduced expectations of a near-term US interest rate hike and improving global risk sentiment. Data [USN:L6N45Q03T TEXT:"showed"] Gulf oil flows excluding Iran surged to over 81% of pre-war levels in September, led by a recovery in Saudi exports. The recovery came despite attacks on the kingdom's oil infrastructure and a wave of Iranian strikes on regional shipping. Iran's own exports, meanwhile, fell to zero under a US blockade. Saudi Arabia stocks led the gains, with the benchmark index (.TASI) up 0.4%. Al Rajhi Bank (1120.SE) rose 0.6% and oil giant Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) climbed 1%. Developments in Yemen also supported sentiment. Saudi Arabia said Saudi-backed Yemeni forces advanced on Monday to [USN:L1N45R06H TEXT:"recapture"] coastline along the Bab el-Mandeb Strait up to the port city of Mocha, pushing Iran-aligned Houthi forces out of most areas seized last month. Elsewhere in the region, gains were small. The Qatari index (.QSI) added 0.2% and Dubai's main share index (.DFMGI) edged up 0.1%. US data added to the upbeat mood. Bets on a US rate hike in October faded after data released on Friday showed job growth slowed more than expected in September, while nonfarm payrolls for the previous two months were revised lower. Traders have not given up on tightening, however. CME's FedWatch Tool shows an 87% chance of a rate increase in December. Gulf markets tend to track shifts in US monetary policy expectations as most regional currencies are pegged to the dollar. Abu Dhabi bucked the regional trend, with its stock index (.FTFADGI) down 0.1%.

item.title: Spain expected to approve housing decrees that triggered snap election
item.description: Spain's government is set to approve on Tuesday two housing decrees whose rejection by parliament last week prompted Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to call a snap election, Culture Minister Ernest Urtasun said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spain's government is set to approve on Tuesday two housing decrees whose [USN:L1N45O0BD TEXT:"rejection by parliament"] last week prompted Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"to call a snap election"], Culture Minister Ernest Urtasun said. The decrees will then be sent for approval by a reduced body of caretaker lawmakers who remain in place after parliament was dissolved ahead of the November 29 election, state broadcaster TVE said. The standing body of 69 members, when including lower house speaker Francina Armengol from Sanchez's Socialist Party, has a slim majority in favour of the measures, which include rent caps, a temporary ban on evictions and limits on corporate purchases of residential property, according to state broadcaster TVE. The decrees would be implemented temporarily until a new parliament is formed, TVE said. Urtasun told reporters on Monday the decrees would have some small variations but no major changes compared to those approved by the cabinet but rejected by parliament last week. "In terms of protection, they will certainly be on a par with, or even exceed, what we agreed last time," Urtasun said. Sanchez, who will hold a press conference after the cabinet meeting, said on Monday he needed more seats in parliament after failing to garner enough support for his proposals to address a [USN:L8N45Q06Q TEXT:"housing crisis"] that has drawn nationwide protests following the [USN:L8N45F0PQ TEXT:"attempted eviction"] of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid.

item.title: Former German spy chief detained on suspicion of espionage and treason, Bild reports
item.description: Former German foreign intelligence chief August Hanning has been detained on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power, Bild newspaper reported on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former German foreign intelligence chief August Hanning has been detained on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power, Bild newspaper reported on Tuesday. The report said prosecutors allege Hanning, whose tenure ended in 2005, bought secret information from a former employee of the foreign intelligence agency BND and intended to sell it on as part of his consulting activities. The BND and the office of Germany's federal prosecutor did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. The investigation was launched after the discovery of an alleged leak of intelligence reports intended for the chancellery, Bild said.
